references.text: God makes a covenant with Noah and instructs him to enter the ark together with his family.
God commands Noah to enter the ark with his entire household because of his righteousness.
Repeats that Noah, his three sons, his wife, and his sons' three wives entered the ark on the same day.
Jesus compares his return to the days of Noah, when people lived in ignorance until the flood came and took them all away.
By faith Noah built the ark in reverence for God, and through it his household was saved.
Noah and his family—eight souls—were saved through water, a type of baptism.
God did not spare the ancient world but preserved Noah and seven others as a preacher of righteousness when he brought the flood.
A complementary event confirming the completeness of God's salvation of Noah's household.
New Testament allusion using Noah's entry as a type for the final judgment.
Prophetic parallel linking the flood to the final judgment.
Continuation of the same event, expanding the scope of salvation to all living things.
